name: Devbox
description: Reproducible, per-project development environments powered by Nix packages without requiring users to write Nix expressions.

Download Jetify's installer to a temporary file and inspect it instead of piping network content directly into a shell. Ask separately before installing Nix, enabling or reconfiguring the Nix daemon, using administrator privileges, creating WSL2, editing a shell startup file, adding global packages, downloading a large closure, or overwriting project configuration. Never run an unfamiliar project's init hook or script during installation. Do not update a lock file, change flake trust, enable experimental Nix features, pass `--allow-insecure`, garbage-collect the Nix store, delete profiles, or remove `.devbox` data without explicit approval. If prerequisites are unsupported, stop and link to the closest official installation path.

Verify `devbox version`, `nix --version`, the resolved executable path, platform mode, Nix daemon state, and the list of profiles before and after setup. For an existing project, inspect configuration without evaluating hooks. Otherwise initialize a disposable empty directory, inspect the generated JSON and lock file, enter an empty Devbox shell, and exit without adding packages. Prove that no pre-existing project lock, global profile, shell file, daemon setting, or store path was removed. Finish with changed paths, downloaded store size, verification evidence, manual steps, and rollback commands that remove only setup-created files and restore backups.

setup.preserve: all existing Nix profiles, channels, flakes, daemon configuration, trust settings, store paths, Devbox global state, project devbox.json and devbox.lock files, .devbox directories, shell startup files, environment variables, init hooks, scripts, and cached packages

name: act

Preserve `.github/workflows`, local actions, `.actrc` files at XDG, home, and repository scope, event payloads, variable files, secret files, Docker contexts, images, containers, volumes, caches, and artifact directories. Apply only the requested runner image, container architecture, artifact path, or container reuse behavior.

Treat every workflow and referenced action as executable, potentially untrusted code. Stop before running jobs, pulling large runner images, mounting the Docker socket, using host networking, running privileged containers, writing artifacts, contacting external services, or reusing a container. Never put token values on the command line or in shell history. If a GitHub token is required, use only the opaque `secret://github/token` reference through act's secure prompt or a permission-restricted temporary secret file, and remove only that setup-created file afterward. Do not infer production secrets from GitHub CLI, environment variables, or repository files.

Verify the installed version and executable provenance, parse help output, list workflows and jobs without execution, and show the exact event, workflow, job, runner image, mounts, network mode, and secret names that a later approved run would use. Confirm that no job ran, no image was pulled, no container or volume was created, and no workflow, `.actrc`, credential, Docker context, or artifact changed. setup.install: Install a checksummed act release through a documented package-manager channel, then detect the active Docker-compatible API without starting or reconfiguring a container engine.
setup.preserve: all workflows, local actions, layered .actrc files, event and variable files, secret files, Docker contexts, images, containers, volumes, caches, and artifact directories

Detect Windows 10+, macOS 12+, or Debian 12, architecture, package managers, existing OpenBoard or Open-Sankoré installation, document library, profiles, caches, interactive displays, pen tablets, projectors, dual-screen layout, cameras, microphones, media backends, virtual printers and file associations. Install only the current stable official package for the supported platform and architecture. Do not select a development branch, community package for an officially supported platform, or migrate legacy libraries without approval.

Install without starting a lesson, creating a board document, opening the library or changing handlers for UBZ, UBX or PDF files. Preserve every document, page, annotation, embedded resource, background, thumbnail, folder, trash item, favorite, widget, podcast, recording, cache, preference, toolbar, pen setting, calibration and recent item. OpenBoard may maintain its document library rather than asking for a normal Save operation; never assume closing a test document leaves storage untouched. Inventory library paths and hashes before any functional launch.

Printable-file, PDF, UBZ and UBX import can create converted documents and extracted assets; export, duplication, rename, move and deletion can alter the library. Do not import or export real teaching material merely to test installation. Treat web widgets as remote applications: they can run JavaScript, store cookies, follow links, download files and display private or untrusted content. Never add a widget, enable cookie persistence, sign in, capture a web page, trust a certificate, grant browser permissions or expose student data. Desktop mode, region capture and page capture can record other applications, notifications and credentials.

Podcast recording can capture the board, microphone and system media into persistent files. Do not request microphone, camera, screen-recording or accessibility access; do not start a recording or select an output folder. Preserve display arrangement, projector resolution, pen mapping and interactive-whiteboard calibration, and never install hardware drivers or recalibrate a classroom device for verification. Verify publisher or package provenance, checksum when provided, package version, executable, bundle files, supported platform and data locations from package metadata without launching the normal GUI. Confirm no document, cache, handler, cookie, capture, device grant, calibration, media file, process or network connection changed. Roll back only the installed application and setup-owned shortcuts.

setup.install: Install the current stable official OpenBoard package for a supported platform without launching a lesson, creating documents, changing file handlers, migrating legacy data, configuring devices, adding widgets, or granting capture permissions.
setup.preserve: all documents, pages, annotations, resources, backgrounds, thumbnails, folders, trash, favorites, widgets, recordings, caches, preferences, toolbars, pens, calibrations, displays, handlers, virtual printers, recent items, and legacy libraries
setup.safety: Never import, convert, export, move or delete teaching material; run web widgets; persist cookies; capture screens; record audio or video; expose student data; install drivers; or recalibrate devices without an exact scope preview and approval.
setup.verify: Verify provenance, checksum, package version, executable, bundle, platform and data locations without the normal GUI, then prove no library, cache, handler, cookie, capture, grant, calibration, media, process or network state changed.
